response.why: It's still upkeep before my main phase; passing now lets me play Riverpyre Verge first (5th land) then flash in the now-cheap Eddymurk Crab (~3 mana after graveyard reduction) with mana left over for Opt/Spell Snare/Burst Lightning, which is strictly better sequencing than casting anything with only 4 lands right now.
response.plan: Pass through upkeep/draw, play Riverpyre Verge in main phase, then cast Eddymurk Crab (cheap from graveyard fill) while holding remaining mana for instants; Torch the Tower can't kill their 4/5 Hearth Elemental alone so save it for a smaller threat or combine with other removal.

response.why: Most lines leave the board even (my 5/5 Crab + 4/5 Hearth Elemental vs their tapped Hearth + 5/5 Crab), so I favor whichever response chips their life or strips a card (Spell Snare countering their cheap Harmonize recursion is best); the Sunderflock branch is clearly worse since it gives them a third 5/5 body I have no answer to this turn.
response.plan: Let Hearth Elemental resolve, hold Spell Snare for their cheap (MV2) recastable spells like the Harmonize-cost Glacial Dragonhunt, and use Burst Lightning/Torch reactively rather than pre-emptively since no target is currently worth killing (all their creatures have 5 toughness).

response.why: Attacking with just Eddymurk Crab (hold Hearth Elemental back) is safest: worst case is an even trade with their Crab, but if they block with the summoning-sick Hearth Elemental instead, my Crab kills it for free and survives; attacking with the Hearth Elemental risks losing it to their Crab block for nothing.
response.plan: Attack with Eddymurk Crab only, holding both Hearth Elementals back as blockers; keep Spell Snare/Burst Lightning available for their turn.

response.why: Dominant position either way (opp at 5 life, we hold 2 tapped 5/5s that untap next turn plus an active 4/5 blocker/attacker) — anchors near 'unstoppable clock'. Harmonizing the graveyard draw spell nets extra cards (our hand 2 vs opp 0-1) for only a small defensive cost (tapping Hearth Elemental), since opponent's lone possible attacker this turn (Eddymurk Crab 5/5, Sunderflock still sick) can't meaningfully threaten us at 12 life, and we still hold enough mana up for Spell Snare either way.
response.plan: Prefer casting the graveyard draw spell via Harmonize (tapping Hearth Elemental if needed) to dig for more gas while keeping Spell Snare mana open; next turn swing with both Crabs + Hearth Elemental into their 2 blockers for likely-lethal or near-lethal damage.

response.why: No-blocks leaves us at exactly 0 life = an immediate loss (score 0).
